items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Now Gerry, letting me into his band was a big moment for me. Because I stayed with the band for three years, I re-joined the band eighteen years later and stayed for another year or so

ctx.x: Very much so. I came into the business with the ability to play the trombone. I played a Broadway show, I did the music hall, I did the operas and the classical music. I did do Larry Elgart, on bass trombone by the way so I was playing first trombone on the classical end of it and I was playing bass trombone on the jazz end let’s say, not really jazz at that point but on the dance band end of it. When — a tremendous milestone was Gerry Mulligan. I remember walking, I was at the union and Dick Hickson, who is a…

jazz band.” I said, “Well I’m quick.” He says, “Come on down.” That was it. That was the end of the conversation. I went down to the rehearsal. I sat next to Brookmeyer. Now Gerry, letting me into his band was a big moment for me. Because I stayed with the band for three years, I re-joined the band eighteen years later and stayed for another year or so, and musically it was a wonderful experience. Brookmeyer was the person in my life that I learned the most from. Sitting next to Bob. I always prided myself on my…
Sorry to interrupt, is that what you mean by playing outside your instrument?
